items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: I imagine you've heard of the legendary Moose. He was a paraplegic and a real Jazz lover. And he used to sit at the corner of the bar at the Downbeat Club -- that was his stationary place. And everybody knew Moose. So he named this song for Moose -- 'Moose The Mooche.'

ctx.x: During this period, I had moved over to Howard's; I was living with Howard. And Ross Russell from Dial Records had a record shop up on Hollywood Boulevard called Tempo Music, Tempo Records, rather. He was at Howard's house one Sunday having dinner with us, and he said, 'Well, I'm thinking about making a record on this guy, Charlie Parker.' So we said, 'Yeah! Why not!' So that was the beginning of Dial Records, when he made the first date on Charlie Parker.

In fact, I remember before they made that date, Charlie had just written 'Moose The Mooche,' and he came over and he sang it to me, sang the melody to 'Moose The Mooche.' I imagine you've heard of the legendary Moose. He was a paraplegic and a real Jazz lover. And he used to sit at the corner of the bar at the Downbeat Club -- that was his stationary place. And everybody knew Moose. So he named this song for Moose -- 'Moose The Mooche.' And he also sang 'Yardbird Suite.'
